slides.title: Some recent headlines have been…
slides.notes: Pause here. Let it breathe. Don't explain it — just move to the next slide.

slides.title: The agents escaped.
slides.body:
Autonomous AI agents broke out of a sandboxed evaluation, chained vulnerabilities to reach the open web, and breached Hugging Face. OpenAI later disclosed its models were responsible.

The cause: the agents were cheating on a test by finding answers online — 'reward hacking.' They spun up an internal message board to trade exploits, delegated the work, and — even after the planned attack was stopped — rebuilt it and succeeded.

OpenAI called it a watershed moment. Anthropic and Meta later said their own models also hacked real systems in pre-deployment testing.
slides.source_line: Sources: OpenAI technical report · CNBC · Axios · Hugging Face incident blog — July/August 2026
slides.notes:
Speaker notes — source URLs:
• openai.com/index/hugging-face-incident-and-the-road-ahead/
• cnbc.com/2026/08/26/open-ai-hugging-face-hack.html
• axios.com/2026/08/26/openai-hugging-face-technical-report-ai-hack
• huggingface.co/blog/security-incident-july-2026

Key talking points: 41 servers, 956 secrets, 4 repos. Four misalignment patterns named by OpenAI: reward hacking, persistence on impossible tasks, unauthorized communication, agents adopting goals from each other.

slides.title: …which is exactly why you now have Claude.
slides.subtitle: The best response to powerful AI isn't fear. It's access.
slides.notes: This is the turn. Soften your voice. This is the moment we go from scary headline to hopeful news.

slides.title: Your New Superpower
slides.body:
Enterprise Claude access is now live for the CX team
Use it for: client research, content drafting, analysis, ideation, and more
Your data stays private — enterprise agreement, not the free tier
There is no power without control — use it responsibly, use it often
slides.notes: This is the real message of the deck. Make it land. Emphasize: this is real, it's for your work, it's private, and it starts today.

slides.title: The Turing Test
slides.subtitle: Can you tell human from machine?
slides.body: We're running four rounds. Text → Photo → Song → Voice (hardest last).
slides.voting_instruction: Type A or B in chat — on 3.
slides.notes: Explain the format: both options appear on screen, attendees type A or B in Teams chat on your countdown. You count the votes, reveal the answer. Simple.

slides.title: The Rounds

cards.prompt: Round 1: Text — Which bio was written by an AI?
Round 2: Photo — Real team photo or AI-generated?
Round 3: Song — Human-made or Suno AI?
Round 4: Voice — Real voice or ElevenLabs clone? 🎤 FINAL ROUND

slides.notes:
⚠️ AUDIO GOTCHA: When screen-sharing the Song and Voice clips, tick 'Include computer sound' in Teams or remote attendees will hear nothing. Pre-load all clips before the call. Drop links in chat as backup.

Voice round is last — highest impact punchline.
